title: Report mode accepts a quoted root ending in a backslash instead of hanging in an interactive window
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: The app did not exit within 7000 ms (7011 ms) on ["...\trailing\" --report "...\trailing-report.json"], while the control without the trailing backslash exited 0 with a report after 1823 ms. Report written: False.

C1: A quoted root ending in a backslash followed by --report (e.g. "<tree>\" --report "<r>", from cmd, Start-Process or ProcessStartInfo.Arguments) starts report mode, writes the report and exits 0 instead of opening an interactive window that never exits: missing
C2: The repaired root is the folder the user named (X\), and the report it writes matches the control's (same core.status and core.files for the same tree): missing
C3 (SC-028): a report path in a folder the account cannot write is refused up front with exit 3, before any scan, so the comment 'every refusal exits at once' (App.xaml.cs:30) is true: missing
C4 (SC-028/SC-037): the up-front write probe is created new (CreateNew, DeleteOnClose), so it cannot follow a link already at the probe name: missing
C5 (SC-037): the report's temporary file cannot be redirected by a link planted during the scan (a fresh, unpredictable name opened CreateNew, and Discard tracks that name): missing

An odd run of 2n+1 backslashes before a quote in a repaired line is kept whole, as typed. The alternative is n+1, treating the escape as undone. Both resolve to the same folder through Win32, but the report's "root" carries the extra backslashes under the chosen rule.
Rule 3 leaves out the proposal's `new StreamWriter(` and `.AppendText(` patterns, because they match correct code. A reviewer may prefer them back, together with an except list.

The name source is a Func<string> injected through an internal constructor rather than an injected IFileSystem or a stored stem. This was chosen as the smallest seam that lets a test plant a link at the exact temporary name.

The single-file published exe was not rebuilt for this attempt: the change is one string comparison in Core, and the Debug apphost exe facts (same code, real entry point) pass. Attempt 1 already measured the published exe on the repaired shapes.

A piece of a quoted report path that ends in a quote (a report path typed ending in a backslash, such as `"C:\out --old\"`) is still taken for a damaged root by the root branch of the exposed-token check and refused. That path is a folder, so the app would refuse the report path anyway (exit 3), and the obligation does not name it; filing it, not building it.

deviation: Added the public const CommandLine.ReportOption and made App.ReportOption read it. The obligation allowed `argument == "--report"` or a set of option names passed in; the App's option spelling is private to App.xaml.cs and Core cannot see it, so a second literal would be a copy that could drift.

critique missed: The design's gate opens whenever argv holds any '"', including a trailing-only quote, and the REPAIR tokeniser toggles quoting on every '"'. The critique never asked what happens when Windows' split is already correct and one unpaired backslash-quote remains, e.g. `D:\Data\" --report out.json` (no opening quote). That line ran report mode on the base. On the repaired build it became one argument, --report disappeared, and the exe hung with its window up. A check could be written from it: for every line where shell32's argv is not merged, Arguments must keep --report as an element, or fall back to argv.

critique missed: The design carried 'the probe needs exactly the rights the real write needs' as a must-verify precondition. The M3 triage and its critic note then dismissed measuring it, on the reasoning that a folder refusing one refuses the other. Windows grants DELETE to the creating open (DeleteOnClose), so a create-only folder (inherited Deny DELETE on files plus Deny FILE_DELETE_CHILD on the folder) passes the probe. File.Move then fails and leaves .fsa-*.tmp, so the app scans the whole root and exits 3 at the end. A single TempTree.Deny experiment would have shown it before build.

critique missed: The design and the Arguments docstring say the program name is skipped 'by the CRT rule', but the spec'd rule (a quoted name ends at its first closing quote, an unquoted name at the first space) is not ucrt's, which flips quoting on every '"'. The critique accepted the spec without comparing it to ucrt. A legal partly quoted exe path (`<dir>\"a b"\FsAnalyser.App.exe ...`) fails alignment and is refused with exit 2.

critique missed: m1's prescribed widening of the 'decides its mode only on repaired arguments' rule to `\b\w+\.Args\b` still needs a word character before the dot. `e?.Args`, `e!.Args` and `(e).Args` read StartupEventArgs.Args before the repair and pass the rule. The critic's note on the fix filed other spellings but not these.

critique missed: The write-opener rule, even after m6's type-level ban (StreamWriter, FileStream, File.Open, the parameterless .Create/.OpenWrite/.CreateText/.AppendText), lets File.AppendAllBytes(Async), File.Copy(src, dst, overwrite) and FileInfo.CopyTo(dst, true) through. File.Copy was measured overwriting a sentinel through a hardlink and through a file symlink at the destination, which is SC-037 again at the one predictable name <report>.

critique missed: The design's own contract lists a new exit 2 (Arguments returns null) that happens before the report path is read and deletes nothing. Its only WindowReport.cs change was an Exit 3 sentence, so the exit-code contract that App.xaml.cs:11 points to stayed stale. Its sentence 'Every non-zero exit leaves no file at <file>' is untrue for the no-value exit 2 and for this one.

Running tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1 against HEAD settles it.

still unknown: Which root does the interactive window show for `"<tree>\"` alone on the published exe? Three validators saw only that a window was alive with a non-zero MainWindowHandle after 3 s. The root value rests on CommandLineTests rows plus RootArgument. UI Automation is refused on this host (lesson #888), so it needs a startup-hook readout from a path launch.

still unknown: Does argv still equal the ucrt split of GetCommandLineW on other Windows builds or ucrtbase versions? It was measured only on Windows 11 10.0.26300 with ucrtbase 10.0.26100.9711 (N-065). If it diverges, `"X\" --report f` falls back to null and the app exits 2 instead of writing a report.

still unknown: Does a real second principal planting at the report folder mid-scan behave like the same-account plants measured here? Every plant was made by the runner's own account, and the fresh .fsa-<hex>.tmp name could only be planted through an injected stem in unit rows.

still unknown: Does an unattended whole-drive run of `C:\ --report <writable path>` run to completion and write the report on the published exe? Only the up-front refusal on C:\ was measured (exit 3 in 145-152 ms).

went wrong: The IN-M1 fix then created O-053. The builder widened the exposed-option check from the decided `--report` to any token starting with '--', and the docstring called such a token 'unmistakable', which was false. A valid line `"D:\Data\" --report "C:\out --old\r.json"` exited 2 although attempt 1 had handled it. Found by code-review #3 and validate #3, it cost build #3 and two more reviews. The widening was declared as a deviation but not challenged at build.

went wrong: The probe-rights precondition (O-042) was reasoned away at triage instead of measured, and was then disproved by a reviewer and a validator on a create-only drop folder. SC-028's promise that every refusal exits at once was false for that folder until build #2.

caused_by.reason: Trip 1 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 1 fork that only a measurement can settle. O-019: unsettled design fork: On the shipped apphost (single-file Release and the Debug apphost), does e.Args equal the ucrt-rule split of GetCommandLineW after argv0 for the finish-line lines: `"<f>\" --report "<r>"`, the spaced pair, `"<f>\"` alone and `"<f>\" extra --report "<r>"`? Its context: The design assumes yes: the investigation measured .NET argv equal to CommandLineToArgvW on these shapes. If no, the alignment check sends these lines to the fallback, so finish lines 1, 2 and 4 exit 2 instead of passing, and the parser contract must change (for example, align on CommandLineToArgvW, or drop alignment and trust the argv0 skip). The queued spike getcommandlinew-retokenise-restores-report-args settles it. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: MEASURE IT; do not build it. This is a measurement that needs no fix and no change to src/. The risk spike runs it on the two shipped hosts as they are. SETUP - Set TAAD3_HOME to a new empty scratch folder. - Keep all scratch, including the probe project, outside the repo tree (lessons #889, #412). - Put trees and report folders under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp (lesson #360). - Build the Debug apphost: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj`. This gives bin/Debug/net10.0-windows/win-x64/FsAnalyser.App.exe. - Publish the single-file Release exe into a scratch folder WHOSE PATH CONTAINS A SPACE, so the quoted-argv0 skip is exercised: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App/FsAnalyser.App.csproj -c Release -o "<scratch>\pub dir"`. - The probe is a scratch startup-hook assembly, loaded with DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS the way FsaWindowHook already drives the published exe. Inside the real app process, before Main, it writes one JSON file (path taken from an env var) and then calls Environment.Exit(0), so no window opens and nothing is scanned. The JSON holds: (a) GetCommandLineW, the raw line; (b) Environment.GetCommandLineArgs(), whose [1..] is e.Args (WPF StartupEventArgs); (c) the real ucrt split of this process's own line: P/Invoke ucrtbase `_configure_wide_argv(1)`, then `__p___argc` / `__p___wargv`; (d) shell32 CommandLineToArgvW(GetCommandLineW); (e) a scratch reference of the design's FAITHFUL tokeniser and CRT argv0 skip, applied to (a). LINES, each on both hosts: - L0, the control: `"<f>" --report "<r>"` - L1: `"<f>\" --report "<r>"` - L2: `"<f sp>\" --report "<d sp>\out dir\r.json"`, with two spaces - L3: `"<f>\"` alone - L4: `"<f>\" extra --report "<r>"` ROUTES - ProcessStartInfo.Arguments on every line, both hosts. - Start-Process with a single -ArgumentList string, and `cmd /c` with an unquoted exe path (Debug host only, no space in its path), on L1 and L2. INCONCLUSIVE (rerun; this does not decide the fork) if any of these happens: - L0's (b)[1..] is not the 3 tokens; - L1 does not show the one merged argument; - the hook did not run in the shipped single-file exe. HOW THE RESULT DECIDES 1. On every line, host and route, (b)[1..] equals (c)[1..], and (e) equals (b)[1..]: the answer is YES. The design stands as written. The build aligns with the FAITHFUL emulator on the ucrt rule, and there is no resynthesis. 2. (b)[1..] equals (c)[1..] but (e) differs: the emulator spec is wrong in one branch. Record which branch (argv0 skip, backslash-run counting, empty token). The design is rewritten to fix that branch and keeps ucrt alignment. 3. (b)[1..] differs from (c)[1..] but equals (d)[1..]: alignment moves to CommandLineToArgvW, a shell32 import in Core.Native, and the design is rewritten. 4. (b)[1..] matches neither (c) nor (d) on some line: a split of the raw line cannot be the alignment check. The design is rewritten to drop alignment and rely on the argv0 skip plus the gate, with that line recorded as the counter-example. Also record, for the gate premise: whether (b) holds a '"' on L1, L2 and L4, and only a trailing '"' on L3. Nothing has measured this yet. - The investigation compared .NET argv with CommandLineToArgvW under pwsh.exe. That is neither the shipped single-file host nor the Debug apphost. - Nobody has compared argv with the ucrt rule, which is what the design's alignment check actually uses. - The queued spike getcommandlinew-retokenise-restores-report-args has no verdict. It also presumes a FIX build, and this fork does not need one. The synthesis marked the losing answer as forcing a re-synthesis. If alignment fails on these lines, finish lines 1, 2 and 4 exit 2, and the alignment contract has to move to CommandLineToArgvW or be dropped. So the answer has to come before build, not during it. The critique's own fix for M3 asked for exactly this lap. The hook-plus-dump probe measures the real shipped binaries and changes nothing in src/. Its worst case is a few short-lived processes and some KB of scratch, so it is a small experiment the spike can run on this machine without a person. A measure lap is available: 0 of 2 have been used. The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.

caused_by.reason: 1 obligation(s) landed on this stage after it passed (O-045), so nothing downstream was ever going to carry them out and the merge would have refused. Sent back with what raised them: O-045 (fix): IN-M1 (major): The input is an unpaired backslash-quote, for example `D:\Data\" --report out.json` (no opening quote). Windows splits it cleanly into [D:\Data", --report, out.json]: the only damage is the root's trailing quote. The gate opens on that quote and the FAITHFUL split matches, so Arguments returns the REPAIR split. REPAIR toggles quoting on every '"', so it opens a quoted part that Windows never opened, and that part runs to the end of the line. The result is ONE argument, <D:\Data\ --report out.json>. App.OnStartup (App.xaml.cs:29) then finds no --report and opens the interactive window on a nonsense root. That window never exits. On the base this exact line ran report mode with root RootArgument("D:\Data\"") = D:\Data\. So the slice brings back its own hang for a line that used to work, against the design's contract that a line is 'never re-split wrongly'. Measured on the Debug apphost: `<tree>\" --report <r>` was still running with its window up after 6000 ms and wrote no report. The control `<tree>\ --report <r>` exited 0 in 811 ms. Other members of the family behave the same way: - `D:\Data\" --report "out.json` gives one argument; - `D:\Data\" --report "C:\out\" x` gives one argument; - `app.exe D:\Data --report C:\out\" ` gives `C:\out\ ` with the trailing space absorbed. Fall back exactly as for a failed alignment (argv when every quote is trailing, otherwise null) in either of two cases: - the typed line after the program name holds an odd number of '"', so the repair would end inside an unterminated quoted part; - argv has a "--report" element that the repaired list lacks. The repair exists to split what Windows merged, and must never hide an option that Windows' split exposed. Do NOT simply drop an odd-run quote that stands outside quotes. That breaks the batch idiom `%~dp0"data" --report out.json` (`C:\scripts\"data" ...`), which the repair currently gets right: [C:\scripts\data, --report, out.json]. CLOSE THE CLASS, NOT THIS INSTANCE. IN-M1 is one member of "backslash-quote outside a quoted part, which the repair pairs with a later quote or leaves open, joining arguments Windows split" (members come from ordinary input, by accident). Enumerate the class into a corpus committed with the code -- a table of inputs, fire/quiet plant rows, an alias list, a census of every type that carries the value -- in the repository or .taad/slices/SL-007/, make every row pass, and show the code before your fix failing the rows you claim to close.
